simple.meaning: מַהְלֵךְ (mahlêk) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a walking (plural collectively), i.e. access.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.

simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.full: H4108. mahlek [ מַהֲלָךְ ] noun masculine Neh 2:6 walk, journey, going (late); construct מַהֲלַךְ Ezek 42:4 2 t.; suffix מַהֲלָֽכְךָ Neh 2:6 ; plural מַהְלְכִים Zech 3:7 ; — 1 walk 'of 10 cubits' breadth before the chambers' in Ezekiel's temple Ezek 42:4 (compare Da). 2 journey from Babylonian to Jerusalem Neh 2:6 ; of dimension of Nineveh, a journey of three days Jonah 3:3 i.e. diameter or length, compare 3:4 ; (according to Herodot see 58 one day's journey = 150 stadia, = length of Nineveh according to Diod ii.3 ). 3 plural goings , i.e. free access (VB) Zech 3:7 .
